content_html_sanitized:
The rest of this article is not a joke, but a description of a farce, the Canadian cannabis situation. I rush to add that this farce is far superior to the tragedy to the south.

The last few weeks have seen cannabis prohibition here suffer hit after hit, but there still seems to be very little understanding of the situation, even in the anti-prohibitionist media, (not a contradiction in terms in Canada.)

So let's begin by putting all of this in context.

So here we are.

Alan Young, the Ottawa law professor who handled this case, is quoted in the Globe and Mail as saying, " We feel it will be appealed, but it's the light at the end of the tunnel ...I can't really see the law maintaining any operation after this year. It's sitting on a really precarious foundation. "

However, there is no indication that the Canadian government has any real understanding of the problems in coming up with a medical cannabis program in the context of prohibition. By comparison, drawing up laws to legalize or decriminalize would be relatively simple.

To make matters even worse, those who draw up a medical cannabis program are going to have to know something about it, and then think about it. That violates all the rules.

It is alright for a politician to admit that he or she or it has smoked and even inhaled, but I defy anyone to find any politician who can display any evidence that they have ever had an informed thought on the subject, with the exception of the Canadian Senators whose report was ignored by the government, because they couldn't even think about legalization.

When Dr. Lester Grinspoon said at the conclusion of Marihuana, The Forbidden Medicine that the full medical potential of cannabis could not be realized under prohibition, he was really commenting on the limitations of politicized medicine.
See
 Live Free or Die In Pain. The Ignorance and Arrogance of the Quacks Who Deny Pain Relief to the Sick and Dying.

This is apt to be an overwhelming problem for Health Canada.

The problem is one of priorities. Which is more important, the well-being of the patients, or the maintenance of prohibition? We certainly know where Ann McLellan's priorities lie. And where she lies
See
 Lies Have Consequences. From Prohibitionist Venom to the Harsh Realities of Life and Death for Patients. Swedish Prohibitionists, Canadian Bureaucracy and DEAland Medical Murder.

Prohibition inevitably has the effect of keeping the price of cannabis much too high, and strict controls on access will have the effect of making it hard for that the poor and the less educated to get it.
See
 World AIDS Day: More Proof That the Suppression Of Medical Cannabis Indeed Cannabis Prohibition Itself Is Mass Murder. Analysis by Richard Cowan

But most of all, the biggest problem is just dealing with the truth about cannabis after decades of lying. That would be a medical miracle.
See
 The Medical Marijuana Problems -- Analysis by Richard Cowan
